| [THEORY-026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md) v4 | For a system driven without feedback through fixed kernels, the average work dissipated at each switch of the drive equals the memory that fails to predict the next input; that is nonnegative when the drive is Markov and, summed, bounds the protocol's dissipation from below when each kernel keeps its equilibrium stationary, so there only nonpredictive memory is wasteful; with feedback, in one binary channel no predictive agent is efficient | Still, Sivak, Bell & Crooks (2012), [LIT-327](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-327.md): β⟨W_diss⟩ for the switch x_t → x_{t+1} equals I[s_t;x_t] − I[s_t;x_{t+1}] (Eq. 14, an identity). | [THEORY-030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-030.md) v3 | For a memory evolving reversibly with its environment, Landauer's bound prices only steps that lose logical distinguishability, at least k ln 2 of entropy per bit lost, exported to the environment and not necessarily as heat, so copying onto a blank register, measuring or evaluating a bit has no minimum cost; learning a label has a floor only in total entropy production, at least the information learnt, which in Goldt and Seifert's perceptron can be paid in the weights' own entropy with vanishing heat | Bennett (2003), [LIT-360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-360.md): the cost attaches to many-to-one maps of the logical state, at least k ln 2 of entropy per bit exported to non-information-bearing degrees of freedom, which "need not" be heat. The record derives it for a memory and environment evolving reversibly from an uncorrelated start: the environment's entropy rises by at least the logical entropy lost, H(X \| f(X)), and an injective step has no floor, attained exactly by a permutation. Goldt & Seifert ([LIT-308](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-308.md)) bound information learnt by total entropy production, payable with vanishing heat in their toy model. It does not license a k_BT ln 2 heat floor per judgment, per gradient step or per bit learnt. Whether the bound survives without reversible dynamics is [QUESTION-215](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-215.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-072](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md) v4 | Organisms differ from dissipative structures such as a candle flame not by far-from-equilibrium self-maintenance, nor by circular self-maintenance alone, but by organisational differentiation: several distinct constraints that produce one another at different time scales | The record's first answer to the demarcation question that [NOTE-094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-094.md) reports. Prigogine ([LIT-516](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-516.md)) supplies the dissipative structures, and nothing in his account separates them from organisms. Mossio, Saborido & Moreno (2009, [LIT-570](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-570.md)) grant a candle flame organisational closure. Its one macroscopic pattern keeps up the conditions of the combustion that makes it. They draw the line at organisational differentiation: in an organism several distinct structures make distinct contributions, where a flame makes "a unique contribution". Montévil & Mossio (2015, [LIT-582](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-582.md)) narrow closure to mutual dependence among constraints. Each constraint must be both produced by and productive of another, with at least one slow and one fast dependence. On the record's reading, that builds differentiation into closure, as Mossio and Bich (2014) already say of closure of constraints. No paper analyses a flame under the 2015 definitions. Neither paper says closure defines an organism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md) v2 | A converged network trained with SGD is not at a point and does not sample its training loss: under a quadratic approximation it samples a Gibbs distribution on a modified loss, isotropic in the Hessian's column space, with probability currents that keep it oscillating, so its speed and spread are set by the learning rate, momentum and batch size | Kunin et al. (2021), [LIT-1011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1011.md), read in [NOTE-711](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-711.md). Modelled as an underdamped Langevin equation with noise covariance proportional to the Hessian, SGD at the end of training converges to a nonequilibrium stationary state: Gibbs on a modified loss whose curvature undoes the Hessian's anisotropy, with inverse temperature S(1 − β²), in broken detailed balance. A ResNet-18 on ImageNet explores isotropically in a plane where the loss is anisotropic, oscillates at Hessian-dependent rates, and moves at the predicted speed across a hyperparameter sweep. For the learned-structure line, a trained solution is in part a property of the regime that trained it. Proposed: the deep-learning evidence is one network, under assumptions the paper concedes are strained. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md) v3 | In the stochastic-differential-equation model of SGD, with a gradient-noise covariance that depends on the parameters, minibatch noise drives the difference of squared norms along a rescaling symmetry, at a rate proportional to learning rate over batch size, to the point on the symmetry orbit where the gradient-noise traces of the two parameter groups are equal, whenever both groups carry noise; so at stationarity SGD neither keeps the difference fixed, as gradient flow does, nor lets it diffuse, as isotropic noise does, and differs from gradient descent by a finite amount however small the noise | Ziyin, Li & Ueda ([LIT-1012](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1012.md), read in [NOTE-714](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-714.md)), with the gradient flow conservation law and the Itô term from Neural Mechanics ([LIT-1013](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1013.md)). If ℓ(u, w) = ℓ(λu, w/λ) for every sample, then under the SDE model of SGD d(‖u‖² − ‖w‖²)/dt = −T(uᵀC₁u − wᵀC₂w), with T = η/S. The noise has no component along the symmetry, but its dependence on the parameters produces a deterministic drift through Itô's lemma. The drift points to the noise-balanced point, and weight decay adds to its rate. In a diagonal linear network the stationary distribution follows exactly: it is non-ergodic, has a memory of initialization, and collapses to zero above a critical temperature. The law is re-derived here (2026-10-19) within the SDE model; the tests are small synthetic networks, and whether it holds in deep networks on real data is QUESTION-164. | Active |
| [THEORY-220](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-220.md) v3 | A far-from-equilibrium system that contributes to its own maintenance has functions relative to itself, with no history or observer needed, and one that switches among self-maintaining processes has indications of success that can be false by its own lights | Bickhard (2000), [LIT-1029](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1029.md), read in [NOTE-729](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-729.md). Function is contribution to a far-from-equilibrium system's own persistence; the asymmetry between persisting and decaying gives function and dysfunction, always relative to the system served, so a parasite's gut serves the parasite and harms the host. A candle flame has functions in this sense. Representation arrives with recursive self-maintenance: a system that picks its next interaction by how it has differentiated its environment implicitly predicates that the interaction will succeed, and can find the predication false. Proposed: a conceptual account, with no model, whose account of having a function (and so of malfunction) is deferred to another paper. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-275.md) v5 | In two optically trapped beads with a symmetric hydrodynamic coupling, one trap moved by a recorded noise drive, time-delayed mutual information and transfer entropy follow the drive's path rather than the coupling's symmetry: the flow between the beads reads two-way under moderate drive, in experiment and numerics, and one-way under strong drive, in numerics of the fitted model only | Das, Manikandan and Banerjee (2025), [LIT-947](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-947.md), read in [NOTE-788](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-788.md). | [THEORY-412](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-412.md) v2 | Driven matter tends toward states that look adapted to the drive, with no replication needed: of two outcomes of a system driven by a fixed external field, equal in internal entropy and in the probability of reversal, the likelier is the one whose formation absorbed work from the drive and dissipated it more reliably | Perunov, Marsland & England (2014; Phys. X 2016), [LIT-518](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-518.md), read in [NOTE-416](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-416.md), on England's macrostate relation ([LIT-515](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-515.md)). | [THEORY-416](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-416.md) | Quantum thermodynamics has at least four inequivalent notions of work, the ensemble average, the two-point-measurement random variable, the ε-deterministic single-shot work content and the resource-theory work, which answer different operational questions; only the two single-shot optima coincide, by identification of formulas and for energy-diagonal states | Vinjanampathy & Anders (2015/16), [LIT-010](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-010.md), read in full in [NOTE-011](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-011.md). | [THEORY-431](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-431.md) | For classical systems with Markovian, microscopically reversible dynamics, the entropy production of a trajectory obeys an exact finite-time symmetry against the time-reversed process, P_F(+ω)/P_R(−ω) = e^ω, wherever ω is odd under reversal; Jarzynski's work equality and the mean second law follow as corollaries, and the symmetry constrains fluctuations, not which steady state a system selects | Crooks (1999), [LIT-522](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-522.md), read in [NOTE-413](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-413.md), with Jarzynski (1997), [LIT-517](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-517.md) ([NOTE-417](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-417.md)), and Seifert's review (2012), [LIT-523](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-523.md) ([NOTE-420](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-420.md)). The work equality ⟨e^{−βW}⟩ = e^{−βΔF} holds at any switching rate, and Crooks derives it from a trajectory-level entropy-production theorem; Seifert derives every known theorem of the kind from one master theorem. | [THEORY-463](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-463.md) | In classical statistical mechanics a strictly irreversible approach to equilibrium cannot come from the isolated Hamiltonian dynamics alone: the fine-grained Gibbs entropy is constant and bounded systems recur, so each account surveyed either weakens the target to typical or long-run behaviour or adds something from outside the dynamics | Frigg & Werndl (2023), [LIT-114](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-114.md), the SEP entry, read in [NOTE-103](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-103.md). | [THEORY-482](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-482.md) | For a closed quantum system that starts thermal and is measured projectively in energy before and after a unitary drive, the two-point-measurement work obeys the Jarzynski equality and the Tasaki–Crooks relation in exactly the classical form, because those energy measurements erase the coherences in which a quantum difference could appear | Vinjanampathy & Anders (2015/16), [LIT-010](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-010.md), read in full in [NOTE-011](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-011.md), which reproduces the derivation (Eqs. 24–30). | [THEORY-517](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-517.md) | Life raises the Earth's entropy production, chiefly by increasing the absorption of sunlight, and if the planet is held at maximum entropy production, the negative feedbacks of that state would give the homeostasis the Gaia hypothesis postulates | Kleidon (2009), [LIT-519](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-519.md), read in [NOTE-423](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-423.md). | [THEORY-532](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-532.md) | Systems pushed from equilibrium develop structures that degrade the applied gradient faster, and living systems and maturing ecosystems are such structures, continuous with convection cells and vortices, so the second law is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for life | Schneider & Kay (1994), [LIT-533](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-533.md), read in [NOTE-415](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-415.md). | [THEORY-679](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-679.md) | For dynamics obeying detailed balance in a heat bath, the heat released in a transition between observer-defined macrostates is bounded below by the log-odds against its reversal less the internal entropy change; where a replicator's likeliest way back is a copy decaying within one generation, the bound grows with the copy's durability and the speed of copying, not with the information copied | England (2012; J. | [THEORY-692](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-692.md) | Near equilibrium, steady states minimise entropy production and every fluctuation decays; far from it, the excess entropy production has no fixed sign, so a fluctuation can grow past an instability of the thermodynamic branch into a structure held up only by flows across the boundary, and thermodynamics supplies only a sufficient condition for such a state's stability, not a principle selecting which structure appears | Prigogine (1977), [LIT-516](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-516.md), read in full in [NOTE-424](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-424.md), with Cross & Hohenberg (1993), [LIT-527](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-527.md), skimmed in [NOTE-418](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-418.md). They decide which of the states the driving allows is reached, and bistability needs them; but the budget they work within is set elsewhere. | Active |
| [THEORY-1250](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1250.md) | A chemostat is an emergent structure of a closed reaction network: when exchange reactions are fast and the reservoir species are abundant by a factor of order Omega, the closed network behaves to leading order as the open one, with its local detailed balance and dissipation, over a window that opens once exchange equilibrates and closes on a time of order Omega, after which a driven network relaxes to equilibrium; neither separation alone suffices | Remlein, Esposito and Avanzini (2026), [LIT-1887](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1887.md), read in [NOTE-1468](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1468.md): a multiscale expansion in the rate ratio ε and a WKB argument in the abundance ratio Ω, for arbitrary stoichiometry. The lifetime scaling was checked by integrating the paper's §IX network, T_δ = 0.00483 Ω against its fit 0.0048 Ω + 0.33. Active. It does not say that every driven closed network departs from open behaviour at T ~ Ω, only that it can from then on, nor anything about systems that are not chemical. | Active |
| [THEORY-1253](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1253.md) | Treating the Bayesian evidence as a partition function with sample size as inverse temperature, the analogue of heat capacity, the rate at which leave-one-out predictive loss falls with sample size, equals half the parameter count in a regular model, as equipartition, and the real log canonical threshold in a singular one, falling below these where prior or discreteness fixes parameters; with multiplicity above one the approach to the singular value is only logarithmic, and the correspondence has no counterpart of physical current or dissipation | LaMont & Wiggins (2019), [LIT-1882](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1882.md), read in [NOTE-1481](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1481.md): the learning capacity C = −N²∂_N U and its equipartition values (Table II, eqs. 16–18, 24, 28, 30). Active: the regular entries were checked by differentiation, and the singular case exactly in K = a²b² ([CASE-152](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-152.md)'s model), where C approaches λ = ½ as ½ − 1/log n, not with the O(1/N) error the paper states. The statistical "temperature" is a sample size, so nothing in the dictionary is a physical heat flow. | Active |
| [THEORY-1261](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1261.md) | At stationarity a driven reaction network is confined to a thermodynamic space: each reaction's affinity lies between zero and the largest cycle affinity per use of that reaction among the elementary flux modes containing it, and each product of concentrations lies between the effective equilibrium constants of the extremal pathways; with no driving the space collapses to the equilibrium point, so multistability, symmetry breaking and amplification above equilibrium need driving and are bounded by it | Liang, De Los Rios and Busiello (2024; PRX 2026), [LIT-1886](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1886.md), read in [NOTE-1463](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1463.md): eqs. 20, 24 and 29, proved for arbitrary stoichiometry from local detailed balance and the conformal decomposition of steady fluxes into elementary flux modes. Checked on the paper's Schlögl parameters and on a reversible rewriting of [CASE-189](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-189.md). Active. It bounds where a stationary state can be, for every choice of kinetics; it does not say which state is reached, whether it is stable, or how long the driving lasts. | Active |
| [THEORY-1264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1264.md) | Far from equilibrium, the weak-noise escape rate from an attractor goes as the exponential of minus system size times a barrier in the quasi-potential, not in any free energy, and that barrier is bracketed by thermodynamics: it is at most the entropy produced in relaxing from the saddle into the attractor and at least minus the entropy produced along the most likely escape path; the two bounds coincide at detailed balance and separate by twice the dissipation of the probability circulation, so far from equilibrium they can be very loose | Santolin, Freitas, Esposito & Falasco (2025), [LIT-1881](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1881.md), read in [NOTE-1465](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1465.md), for overdamped diffusions; Falasco & Esposito (2025), [LIT-1892](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1892.md), §IV.H and appendix A, read in [NOTE-1472](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1472.md), for jump processes with a macroscopic limit. Active: the derivation is two lines from the orthogonal decomposition of the drift and was checked on a linear nonequilibrium diffusion. It does not say that the more dissipative state lives longer, and in the one worked far-from-equilibrium chemical example the bracket is very loose. | Active |
| [THEORY-1265](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1265.md) | Approximating a chemical master equation by a Fokker–Planck or nonlinear Langevin equation gets the quasi-potential right only at the fixed points: between them it mis-estimates the barriers, so escape rates come out wrong by a factor exponential in system size and the approximation can pick the wrong one of two states as the long-run favourite, and its apparent entropy production vanishes at every steady state, missing the dissipation that sustains it | Falasco & Esposito (2025), [LIT-1892](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1892.md), §IV.D–E and §VII.A.1, read in [NOTE-1472](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1472.md); Vellela & Qian (2009), [LIT-1890](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1890.md), appendix A, read in [NOTE-1474](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1474.md). Active: both formulas were checked on the Schlögl model, including Vellela & Qian's counterexample, where the exact and diffusion quasi-potentials favour different states. It does not say diffusion approximations fail near fixed points or for Gaussian fluctuations; there they are exact to leading order. | Active |
| [THEORY-1266](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1266.md) | In an open reaction network of reversible elementary mass-action reactions, sustained currents need an emergent cycle with nonzero affinity: each chemostatted species either breaks a conservation law or opens an emergent cycle, so one chemostat never suffices; with every emergent affinity zero the network relaxes to a unique equilibrium fixed by its unbroken conserved quantities; and a nonequilibrium steady state dissipates exactly the sum over emergent cycles of current times affinity | Rao and Esposito (2016), [LIT-1889](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1889.md), read in [NOTE-1464](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1464.md), with the one-chemostat proof of Dal Cengio, Lecomte and Polettini (2023), [LIT-1897](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1897.md) ([NOTE-1476](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1476.md)). Active: rank–nullity, Wegscheider's condition and two lines of algebra, checked numerically on a reversible rewriting of [CASE-189](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-189.md)'s first construction, which has a single equilibrium at zero affinity and is bistable only above 3.52 RT. It does not say that a driven network is far from equilibrium, multistable or organized; only that without an emergent affinity it cannot be, and what it costs when it is. | Active |
| [THEORY-1268](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1268.md) | In a nonequilibrium steady state of a thermodynamically consistent Markov jump network, the entropy produced while a current is counted, times the squared relative uncertainty of that count, is at least 2k_B, independent of the counting time, so a current precise to ε costs at least 2k_BT/ε² of dissipation; the 2015 letter proves this within linear response and for single-cycle networks at any affinity, and for many-cycle networks far from equilibrium shows it numerically and states it as a conjecture | Barato & Seifert (2015), [LIT-1885](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1885.md), read in full in [NOTE-1480](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1480.md). Active for the scope stated in the title: the biased walk, the unicyclic formula (A/N) coth(A/2N) and the bound on random four-state networks were checked numerically. It bounds the precision of currents, not of occupations, so it does not price how long a maintained state lasts, and the general multicyclic proof is not in this paper. | Active |
| [THEORY-1270](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1270.md) | Entropy production does not select which of several maintained steady states is the stable one: in the bistable Schlögl model the state the system occupies in the long run can carry either the higher or the lower deterministic entropy production rate, and the mean stochastic entropy production follows whichever state is more probable; in general the most dissipative attractor is the longest-lived only under special conditions, and lifetime tracks relaxation entropy only near detailed balance | Vellela & Qian (2009), [LIT-1890](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1890.md) (§3.3, Fig. 6), read in [NOTE-1474](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1474.md), show the counterexample; Falasco & Esposito (2025), [LIT-1892](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1892.md) (§§III.F, IV.H, VIII.B.6), read in [NOTE-1472](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1472.md), give the general account: minimum entropy production holds only near detailed balance with linear dynamics, and the two maximum principles hold only where relaxation and escape dissipations nearly coincide. Active as a negative result. It does not refute every extremum principle, only those that rank steady states by dissipation alone. | Active |
| [THEORY-1273](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1273.md) | In a driven chemical system with two stable states and a finite number of molecules, each maintained state is metastable: it is left by fluctuation after a time exponential in system size, set by a barrier in a nonequilibrium quasi-potential that closes at the saddle-node, and the long-run share of time in each state is fixed by the parameters and system size, not by the initial condition; the deterministic rate equation, where the initial condition decides, holds only on times short of that escape time | Vellela & Qian (2009), [LIT-1890](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1890.md), read in [NOTE-1474](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1474.md), on the Schlögl model, with Falasco & Esposito's general frame ([LIT-1892](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1892.md), §§III.C, IV.H, VI; [NOTE-1472](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1472.md)). Active: the slow eigenvalue, the barriers, the initial-condition independence and the closing of the barrier at the fold were checked numerically on the paper's model. It does not say which state is the more stable without computing the quasi-potential, and the paper's own large-volume rate formula carries a spurious 1/V factor. | Active |
